title: What Happens If You Drink Lava?
sources: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, Lava Temperature and Physical Properties
Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Thermal Burns and Explosive Water Vaporization
Journal of Thermal Biology, Human tissue response to extreme molten temperatures

lines.text: What actually happens to your body if you try to drink molten lava?
lines.caps: What *happens | if you try | to *drink lava?

lines.text: First, lava is liquid rock heated to over two thousand degrees Fahrenheit.
Before it even touches your lips, the intense radiant heat blisters your face and sears your airway.
lines.caps: Radiant heat | *blisters your face | sears your *airway

lines.text: As the thick glowing rock enters your throat, it instantly incinerates moisture in your esophagus.
When it hits your stomach fluids, water flash-boils into steam, expanding seventeen hundred times in volume.
This creates an explosive internal shockwave, blowing your stomach and esophagus apart from the inside.
At the same time, the lava rapidly cools and solidifies into sharp jagged volcanic glass inside your chest.
Death is virtually instantaneous within seconds.
Lava is not a drink, it is liquid magma.
lines.caps: Lava is *not a drink | it is *liquid rock
